channel.title: An Old Whig on The Anti-Federalist Library
channel.description: Recent content in An Old Whig on The Anti-Federalist Library

item.title: An Old Whig I
item.description: Critiques the Constitution for centralizing too much power in the national government, which would undermine state sovereignty and jeopardize individual liberties.

item.title: An Old Whig II
item.description: Warns that the new government, being distant and removed from the people, would weaken representation and diminish individual influence in the political process.

item.title: An Old Whig III
item.description: Expresses concern that the creation of a standing army under federal control could be used to oppress states and the people, threatening the foundation of republican government.

item.title: An Old Whig IV
item.description: Argues that the executive branch under the proposed Constitution will become far too powerful, overshadowing the legislative branch and disrupting the intended balance of power.

item.title: An Old Whig V
item.description: Criticizes the absence of a Bill of Rights in the Constitution, emphasizing the need for explicit protections to safeguard individual freedoms from potential government overreach.

item.title: An Old Whig VI
item.description: Warns that the broad powers granted to the federal government, particularly in taxation and military control, could lead to unchecked federal power and undermine state authority.

item.title: An Old Whig VII
item.description: Warns that the Senate would become an aristocratic body, disconnected from the people and concentrated with too much power, undermining democratic principles.

item.title: An Old Whig VIII
item.description: Raises doubts about the effectiveness of the proposed checks and balances, arguing that they would be insufficient to prevent the concentration of power in the federal government.
